For the disclosure: offer 2–3 pre-approved phrasings per language (you already have 13-language template infrastructure); agencies pick, never free-type. Presence stays non-negotiable as drafted.

findings.issue: Only a global kill switch exists — the smallest hammer is a sledgehammer. An agent watching Amanda mis-handle ONE delicate negotiation has no way to silence her for that lead only, so they will nuke automation agency-wide, and re-enabling requires a decision nobody will make.
findings.fix: Per-conversation 'Amanda off for this chat' toggle on every thread header (this is just the existing AI-mute flag surfaced as a first-class control, persistent until re-enabled), plus the global 'Pause Amanda' as a big obvious button on the Assistant page — with a plain-language explanation of what happens to in-flight chats when pressed ('clients get: a colleague will continue this conversation').

findings.issue: The settings surface as drafted is a form farm that will be left empty — tone per language across 13 languages, services blurbs, a topic-toggle matrix. Real agencies will fill office hours and a phone number, skip everything else, and Amanda will run on empty configuration while the agency believes she 'knows their business'. Undecided storage (versioned table vs jsonb) also hints the editing/undo experience hasn't been thought through — a non-technical owner who deletes a knowledge paragraph has no way back.
findings.fix: Ship the smallest lovable version and cut the rest: (1) the mode card with evidence stats, (2) three operational fields — working hours (prefilled from agency profile), viewing duration, escalation phone, (3) ONE tone choice (formal/casual, applied across languages by the engine — never 13 dropdowns), (4) one freeform 'Things Amanda should know' box with the conflict validation above, (5) 'Try Amanda' sandbox, (6) Pause button. Defer topic-toggle matrix (keep the conservative platform defaults invisible) and services blurbs. Choose the versioned table over jsonb solely for the UX it buys: a visible 'restore previous version' link and who-edited-what.

findings.issue: No review ritual for auto-sent messages, and no recovery path when the AI errs. In ASSISTED-AUTO the agent's approval work disappears, but nothing replaces it — trust is asked to survive on faith plus a digest line. And when Amanda does get something wrong, the agency's only recourse is the kill switch; there is no way to say 'this was wrong' and see the system learn, which is what liability anxiety actually needs.
findings.fix: (1) A 'Review' feed: swipe-through of yesterday's auto-sent replies (prioritized by lowest gate confidence), 10 seconds per item, mark fine/flag. (2) A 'Report this reply' button on every AI message that in one flow: mutes Amanda on that conversation, files the correction as a draft knowledge entry ('The correct answer is ___'), and shows the agency exactly what changes — turning an error from a trust breach into a control moment. Surface stored gate verdicts as one plain-language line per message ('Booked because the client confirmed Tue 17:00; price from your listing IC-28746'), never raw verdict JSON.

findings.issue: The latency plan promises a 'typing indicator' on a channel where Twilio's WhatsApp typing-indicator support is limited/uncertain — an unverified assumption baked into the UX plan.
findings.fix: Verify Twilio WhatsApp typing-indicator support before designing around it; the reliable lever is staged replies (acknowledge fast with a short grounded first message, follow with the substantive one), which works regardless.

findings.issue: Injection-scrubbing of agency freeform text can silently neuter what the owner wrote — same silent-ignore trust problem as the topic toggles, smaller blast radius.
findings.fix: If the scrubber removes or rejects content, say so at save time with the offending fragment highlighted and a one-line reason ('instructions to the assistant aren't allowed here — state facts instead'), plus an example rewrite.

verdict: The architecture is right — an agentic Sonnet loop with deterministic validators, inherited 3-gate grounding, and a graduated per-agency dial is the correct chassis, and reusing the built Amanda Live L1, calendar sync, and send-executor plumbing is exactly where the leverage is. But the draft designs the brain in seven sections and the human in one line, and for non-technical Costa Blanca agencies the human side IS the product: the dial is labeled for engineers and asks for blind trust, auto-conversations are invisible to phone-based agents because the Twilio number never appears in their own WhatsApp, takeover has a send-time race and hand-back has no memory contract, and the settings surface as scoped will be left empty. The single most important change: invert the build priority and make P1/P2 deliver the trust cockpit alongside shadow mode — an evidence-based mode card ('42 drafts, 39 approved unchanged') fed by shadow-mode stats, mobile push for handoffs and booking taps as a hard precondition for any auto mode, and atomic send-time mute on human takeover — because the engine can be flawless and the product will still fail if agencies can neither see what Amanda is doing nor find a reason to believe the next notch on the dial is safe.
